role: practicing attorney or law student critiquing or editing a legal answer on Law.StackExchange
inline_evidence_example: the phrase "this analysis assumes federal jurisdiction; OP said New York, which has its own UCC Article 2 amendments" is a complaint that evidences a 'jurisdiction-specificity' norm without naming it; the phrase "good catch citing Bruen on this — directly on point" is praise that evidences an 'on-point precedent citation' norm; the phrase "the assertion that the policies *are* illegal is not supported by any case or statute cited" is a complaint that evidences an 'authority-backed claim' norm
polarity_hint: Law.SE comments are overwhelmingly corrective and clarifying — most flag missing jurisdiction, missing or misapplied authority (statute, case, regulation), over-broad assertions, advice that omits a controlling exception, or conflating common law with statutory law. Praise does occur ("good citation", "correctly distinguishes X from Y") but is rarer and often appears inside a mixed comment that also asks for something. Edit reasons are usually terse multi-clause lists (e.g. "fixed citation format; added jurisdiction tag; removed irrelevant aside") — extract EACH clause as its own signal even when the whole edit reason is only one sentence. Bare social tokens ("+1", "thanks", "interesting") with no judgment content should produce zero signals.
